title: Delirium in high-risk geriatric inpatients receiving conservative care: a prospective cohort study
summary:
Older patients often suffer from acute confusion whilst in hospital. This can lead to serious complications and often goes unnoticed, particularly in emergency situations. Our study, conducted at two hospitals in Oldenburg, investigates how frequently and at what stage such acute confusion occurs in older emergency patients. The study is purely observational.
Within 24 hours of admission, a specially trained nurse or a geriatrician will conduct a brief interview to assess whether acute confusion is present. If this is the case, the type of confusion is also determined. During the hospital stay, the nursing staff regularly check for new signs of confusion and inform the study team if necessary. A brief follow-up conversation is then conducted.
Four weeks after discharge, participants or their relatives will be contacted once by telephone to ascertain whether there has been a further hospital admission or admission to another facility, and how many days have been spent at home or in such a facility since discharge.
conditions: Delirium, not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

interventions.name:
Geriatric emergency patients (aged 65 and over) with a negative 4AT score on admission. If delirium is subsequently suspected (Nu-DESC ≥2), a repeat 4AT assessment is carried out. If delirium is diagnosed, a further 4AT assessment is carried out on discharge.
Follow-up: 4 weeks after discharge.

Geriatric emergency patients (aged 65 and over) with a positive 4AT score on admission.
Repeat assessment for delirium using the 4AT on discharge.
Follow-up: 4 weeks after discharge.

Geriatric emergency patients (aged 65 and over) with a negative 4AT score on admission and consistently unremarkable monitoring throughout their stay (Nu-DESC <2).
No further diagnosis of delirium during the stay.
Follow-up: 4 weeks after discharge.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients admitted via the emergency department and classified as requiring conservative (non-surgical) treatment.
This includes patients with an ISAR (Identification of Seniors at Risk) score of 2 or higher on admission.
Exclusion criteria:
The exclusion criteria for the study include aphasia, terminal illness, deafness, an inability to communicate in German, and critical acute conditions such as an unstable heart attack or stroke. Other patients in the oncology department are also excluded.
